description:
FILED s470bm (Opus, 2026-09-05).  PRE-EXISTING.  Found by the Part B item B4
host-leak census (#1172) over perl's own t/, which is the point of that
instrument: `p-my` is not an exported name, so the scan flagged it — and it is
not merely a leak, it is a compiler bug that kills the file.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s470bm/f10.pl, the shape of
`t/io/perlio_open.t:19`):

    use Test::More tests => 1;
    ok((open my $fh, "+>", undef), "opened");

  perl 5.40.3   1..1 / ok 1 - opened
  PCL           dies at LOAD: "Execution of a form compiled with errors"

THE EMISSION:

    (p-void-ctx (pl-ok (p-scalar (p-open (p-my $fh "+>" (p-list-ctx (p-undef)))))
                       "opened"))

`p-my` DOES NOT EXIST.  The runtime has `p-my-=` (the lexical assignment form,
ir-spec §10 "assignment"); there is no `p-my`, exported or internal.  So the
form is a call to an undefined function, SBCL fails to compile it, and the
whole emitted file is dead.

WHAT THE SHAPE IS.  An inline `my` DECLARATION appearing as part of an
expression that is itself a call ARGUMENT.  The declaration should lower as
the handle's binding plus a `p-open` on it; instead `my` became a head and
swallowed `p-open`'s remaining arguments — note that `"+>"` and the `undef`
are now `p-my`'s arguments, not `p-open`'s.

The straightforward spelling is fine, which is why no other instrument sees
this:
    my $ok = open my $fh, "+>", undef;      ->  (p-my-= $ok (p-open $fh …))
It is the extra paren — the declaration inside a call argument — that breaks
it.

WHY NOTHING ELSE CAUGHT IT: the companion suite records the file's verdict, so
this reads as "that file fails", one of many; corpus-diff only compares two
emissions; the gate does not contain the shape.  The leak census asks the one
question that names it — "is every head an op the IR declares?" — and answers
in a second.

BAR when taken: the reproducer runs and prints perl's output; a guard row in a
`Pl/t` file with BOTH spellings (the paren-wrapped one and the plain one, so a
fix cannot regress the working half); `tools/ir-host-leak.pl --list` over
perl's t/ shows no `op:p-my`; corpus-diff explains any diff; the gate.

=== DONE (s470bo) ===

FIXED â and it was TWO bugs, not one.  The reproducer
`ok((open my $fh, "+>", undef), "opened")` needed both.

(1) THE `p-my` HEAD (Pl/PExpr.pm).  `parse()`'s single-element branch unwraps
a `PPI::Statement::Variable` AND strips the declarator, but unwrapped a
`PPI::Statement::Expression` WITHOUT stripping â and which of the two PPI
builds is decided by the run's FIRST token, not by whether it contains a
declarator.  `f((my $q = 3), 4)` is a Statement::Variable and worked;
`f((open my $fh, "<", $p))` is a Statement::Expression, one token later, and
did not: the bare `my` Word reached the operator loop and became a call to the
non-existent op `p-my`, which SBCL could not compile, killing the whole file.
The other two routes into a token run (`parse_expr_to_tree`, `parse_list`)
both strip already, so this was the one that was missing.  The two arms are
merged: stripping the declarator is part of unwrapping.

(1a) AND THE STRIP IS ASYMMETRIC FOR `local` â measured, not guessed.
corpus-diff caught the first version deleting the `local` from
`perl-tests/multideref.t:220` (`eval { @{1, local $x[0][0]} = 1 }`), which on
the Statement::Expression route has its own lowering.  So
`extract_declarations` gained a "which declarators may I strip" parameter and
the unwrap passes `my|our|state` for a Statement::Expression, all four for a
Statement::Variable.  Excluding `local` from BOTH was TRIED and is worse: it
turns `f((local $g = 1))` into a call to a sub named `local`, which dies.
Residue filed as **#1192** (with the finding that `pl-local` is a bogus sub
call on that route, so the family has two wrong answers, one per PPI class).

(2) `open ..., undef` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp).  With `p-my` gone the form ran and
hit the second bug: undef stringified to "" and PCL tried to open the CURRENT
DIRECTORY.  perl's three-argument open with an undef filename opens an
ANONYMOUS TEMPORARY FILE (perldoc -f open).  `%p-open-impl` gains a first cond
clause; `%p-open-anon-temp` creates the file with mkstemp and immediately
UNLINKS it, so it lives exactly as long as the handle, and TMPDIR is honoured
as tmpfile(3) does.

MEASURED mode by mode (open, print, seek 0, readline), 5.40.3 vs PCL after:
    +>  ok print=1 seek=1 read=[hello]   identical
    +<  ok print=1 seek=1 read=[hello]   identical
    >   ok print=1 seek=1 read=[hello]   identical (perl WARNS and still reads)
    >>  ok print=1 seek=1 read=[hello]   identical
    <   ok print=0            read=undef identical (perl warns on the print)
So perl's temp file is O_RDWR whatever the WRITE mode says â a `>` handle
reads its own bytes back, and only `<` is one-directional; the direction map
says so with the probe quoted.  The two advisory warnings are the known
warnings-gated-diagnostic gap (#221); every VALUE matches.

The pipe and dup modes have NO anonymous form â probed: `open($fh,'-|',undef)`
is "Missing command in piped open" (undef, $! = EPIPE) and `open($fh,'<&',
undef)` dies "Can't use an undefined value as filehandle reference" â so the
direction map answers NIL for them and their own clauses keep answering.  NIL
there is an ANSWER, not a swallowed case.

BARS: gate 208 files / 7035 rows with only the 13 known pclxs xs rows failing;
corpus-diff over 111 files IDENTICAL after the `local` asymmetry (the ONE diff
before it was multideref.t, which is what caught it); the 1015-file emission
A/B named io/perlio_open.t as this change's only mover.  Guards: nine run rows
in `Pl/t/census-bugs-01.t` including BOTH declarator spellings (so a future fix
cannot regress the half that always worked) and one row per anonymous-temp
mode, inverse-verified on da5c310 where six of them fail.
subject: `ok((open my $fh, "+>", undef), ...)` emits a call to the NON-EXISTENT op `p-my` and the whole file dies at load - an inline `my` inside a call argument
